questions.prompt: What does a function return if it has no return statement?
questions.explain: Every function hands something back. With no return statement that something is None, which is why a missing return usually shows up as None appearing where a number was expected.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between print(x) and return x inside a function?
choices: There is none, they both give the value back
print shows the value; return hands it back to whatever called the function
return shows the value; print hands it back
questions.explain: print puts characters on the screen and the value is gone afterwards. return gives the value to the caller, which can store it, add to it or pass it on.

questions.prompt: What happens to the lines after a return statement inside a function?
choices: They run after the value is sent back
They never run, because return ends the function
Python refuses to define the function
questions.explain: return leaves the function immediately. Code written after it in the same block is unreachable, which is a common cause of a loop that only ever handles its first item.

questions.prompt: Put these lines in order so the doubled value is printed.
questions.explain: The function has to exist before it is called, the call has to finish before its value can be stored, and only then is there something to print.

questions.prompt: To send a value back out of a function, use the ___ keyword.
questions.explain: return is the keyword that ends the function and hands its value to the caller.
